label: The controlling level contract is structural: Level 1 (<100 LOC) requires spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and implementation-summary.md; Level 2 (100-499 LOC) adds acceptance-criteria.md as the closure gate; Level 3 (>=500 LOC) requires the same set as Level 2.

There is no Level 3+ row in the structural contract; the plan template map carries a level_3_plus entry whose required files equal level_3, and decision-record.md is an add-on created on request at any level, so 3+ names a risk band rather than a distinct file bar.
Level is computed, not guessed: recommend-level.sh scores LOC, file count and risk and judgment may escalate upward, so both commands already hold the value a scaling rule needs.

Level-gated ceremony already exists in both commands: the plan rules require a checklist only for verification_level_2_plus, implement skips step 4 for Level 1, and steps 5.5 and 7.5 are optional for quick fixes under 10 LOC.
plan.md is required at every level, so a plan-side paraphrase always has a document to read and the level question for that check is cost, not availability.
Level 1 takes the paraphrase inline and drops the artifact, severity list and readiness pass, because the document is short while a separate dispatch plus report file is not cheap.

Level 2 makes the pre-coding readiness check the only pre-emptive check, since acceptance-criteria.md verifies outcomes only after the fact, and the verdict can price into the existing plan_clarity 25 points.

At Level 3 and 3+ unresolved design choices are the expensive failure, so the readiness verdict should block rather than advise, and the critic earns its dispatch only when the plan carries competing options or a decision-record exists to audit against.

One rule covers all four levels without a new level concept: paraphrase at every level inside the plan step 5 checkpoint, readiness from Level 2 up inside the existing pre-implementation gate, critic optional from Level 3 up and never gating.
